questions.q: What does the author say success starts with?
a: One product, developed as far as you possibly can
A large portfolio of ideas launched at once
A detailed business plan approved by investors
A strong personal brand built before selling anything
questions.why: Lesson 1 insists that you need one idea executed fully, not many pursued at the same time.

questions.q: What did Bonobos sell during its first year?
a: A single pair of pants in several colors
A full range of suits and golf clothing
Only accessories such as belts and wallets
Custom-made shirts in a few sizes
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Bonobos started with one well-fitting pair of pants and expanded only after reaching $2 million in sales.

questions.q: What does “do things that don’t scale” mean in practice?
a: Give early customers unusually personal attention and service
Avoid automation so the company stays small forever
Refuse to hire anyone until demand forces you to
Focus on one city and never expand beyond it
questions.why: Lesson 2 gives the example of a founder’s personal video message to an early customer.

questions.q: Why is radical transparency valuable for a company?
a: It builds trust, which speeds up innovation and collaboration
It prevents employees from ever disagreeing with leaders
It guarantees that salaries and revenue will rise
It removes the need for managers or feedback
questions.why: Lesson 3 says transparency creates massive trust, the deciding factor in how fast a company can innovate.

questions.q: What happens when you spread yourself across many products at once?
a: You end up with many nearly finished products that never ship
You learn faster because you compare ideas side by side
You reduce risk by diversifying your income early
You attract more customers than a focused competitor
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that dividing your effort produces a pile of almost-there products that consume time and money.
